title: Reading a Data Bit
statement: Let $m,e\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, let $z,w$ be Boolean words, and let $k\le |z|$. On input the self-delimiting pair encoding of $z$ and $w$, there is a finite sequence of access-machine steps from the configuration in state “read data with parameter $e$,” whose four tapes contain the binary words for $0,0,k,2k$ and whose third work-tape head is at $2k$, to a configuration whose state and tapes are determined as follows: if $k<|z|$ and $e$ is true, the state is “answer” with value $m\lor z_k$; if $k<|z|$ and $e$ is false, the state is “bump false”; and if $k=|z|$, the state is “answer false.” The final configuration has tape contents encoding $0,0,k,2k+1$, with the third work-tape head at $2k+1$; the other work-tape heads are at $0$.
